Preview

PREE-vyoo (stress on PREE) · noun

Hear It

What It Means

An early look at something, given before it is open or available to everyone.

The teacher gave us a preview of next week's unit so nobody would be caught off guard.

Worked Example

Members of the fan club attended a special preview of the new roller coaster, riding it while the park's regular visitors still waited outside.

Two things make this a preview: the park arranged it on purpose for a chosen group, and it came ahead of everyone else's turn to ride. Take away either one and a different word would be needed.

How Preview Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

peek

peek: a quick look, often at something hidden

sample

sample: a small piece that shows what the whole is like

Antonyms

review

review: a look back at something after it is finished

replay

replay: a showing of something over again, after it has happened

How Strong Is It? — hint → preview → reveal

hint vs. preview

hint vs. preview: A hint is slighter than a preview: a hint drops only a clue about what is coming, while a preview lets you actually see part of the thing itself early.

reveal vs. preview

reveal vs. preview: A reveal is more complete than a preview: a preview shows a piece of something before it is ready for everyone, but a reveal finally puts the whole thing in full view.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — pre

prefix — pre: before

root — view

root — view: to look at

Put it together

Put it together: Put pre- ('before') together with view ('to look at') and the word builds itself: a preview is a look you get before everyone else does.

Use the root in a new word: review

Use the root in a new word: review: After the museum trip, we wrote a review looking back at what we had seen and judging our favorite exhibits.

Word Choice

A preview is arranged on purpose and comes before something is open or on sale to everyone: a movie preview, a preview of the test topics. You get a preview of something, never at it. For a quick unofficial glance, English reaches for peek instead.
